args.goal: A welcome message for a new volunteer who will moderate an online study group
requirements: names the volunteer's role as study group moderator
gives exactly three first-week steps, numbered
states one boundary of the role (what a moderator does not do)
names where to ask for help
ends with a single question asking the volunteer to confirm a start date
stays under 200 words

description: one-call deliverable against depth on the same rubric

args.goal: A release note for a feature that lets people export their saved notes as a file
requirements: names who the feature is for
says how to start an export in one sentence
names the file format
states one limit of the export
says what happens to the notes after export (they stay)
has a title line of at most eight words

description: one-call deliverable against depth on the same rubric

args.goal: A one-week study plan for a person learning the basics of a new programming language, one hour a day
requirements: lists seven days, one line each
each day names one concrete exercise
day seven is a small project that uses what days one to six covered
names one free resource by its kind (for example official tutorial)
says how the person checks they understood each day
fits one hour a day

description: one-call deliverable against depth on the same rubric (hard: many checkable requirements)

args.goal: A 90-second spoken video script that teaches beginners one way to test a claim they read online
requirements: opens with a hook question in the first sentence
names one specific claim as the running example
gives exactly three numbered steps to test it
each step names a free tool or method by its kind
includes one sentence on a common mistake and how to avoid it
ends with a single call to action that asks viewers to comment one claim
marks each line with a time stamp in seconds from 0 to 90
stays between 200 and 240 words

description: one-call deliverable against depth on the same rubric (hard: many checkable requirements)

args.goal: A question set for a 30-minute interview with a community organizer about how they keep volunteers engaged
requirements: has exactly twelve questions, numbered
groups them under three headings: start, practice, lessons
every question is open (none can be answered yes or no)
at least two questions ask for a specific story with a time and place
one question asks what they would do differently
one question asks for a number they track
no question is longer than 25 words
ends with a closing question that invites anything not covered
